# Graph Layout Algorithms

Reference file for Dimension 2. All citations reference [citations.md](../citations.md). Updated 2026-04-19 with verified Dagre wiki defaults, verified Dagre performance issue data, and explicit library-only vs bundled-with-deps bundle-size disambiguation.

## The Sugiyama Method

All major hierarchical layout algorithms used in workflow editors descend from the method
introduced by Sugiyama, Tagawa, and Toda in 1981 [19]. The algorithm assigns nodes to
horizontal layers with edges directed downward.

### Algorithm Phases

| Phase | Problem | Complexity | Common Approach |
|-------|---------|------------|-----------------|
| 1. Cycle Removal | Feedback arc set | NP-complete | Greedy heuristics [19] |
| 2. Layer Assignment | Assign nodes to layers | Polynomial | Network simplex, Coffman-Graham [19] |
| 3. Dummy Vertex Insertion | Multi-layer edges | O(m) | Replace with path of dummy vertices [19] |
| 4. Crossing Minimization | Minimize edge crossings | NP-complete | Average/median heuristic, layer sweep [19] |
| 5. Coordinate Assignment | Position within layers | Polynomial | Brandes-Köpf (linear time, ≤2 bends/edge) [19] |
| 6. Edge Drawing | Route edges | Varies | Splines or polygonal chains [19] |

Overall time complexity: O(mn) for simplest implementations (n vertices, m edges);
optimized variants approach near-linear time [19].

## Algorithm Comparison

React Flow's official documentation provides this comparison [4]:

| Library | Dynamic Sizes | Sub-flows | Edge Routing | Bundle Size (library-only) | Complexity |
|---------|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|---|
| **Dagre** | Yes | Yes* | No | ~39 KB | Simple |
| **D3-Hierarchy** | No | No | No | ~14 KB | Simple |
| **D3-Force** | Yes | No | No | ~15 KB | Moderate |
| **ELK** | Yes | Yes | Yes | ~1.4 MB | Complex |

\* Dagre has a known issue with sub-flows containing external connections [4].

**Bundle-size measurement disambiguation**: the numbers in [4] are **library-only** figures (what `npm install dagre` or `npm install elkjs` adds to `node_modules`). Pinpoint Engineering's blog [20] reports much larger numbers (d3-hierarchy 136 KB, ELK 7.8 MB) because they measured the **bundled output including transitive dependencies**. Both sets of numbers are accurate in their respective measurement scopes. For decision-making, the library-only sizes are useful for understanding the incremental cost of adding a layout library; the bundled-with-deps figures are useful for estimating the total weight a production bundle will carry. No single "correct" number exists — the right comparison depends on whether other parts of your application already include d3 or its dependencies.

## Dagre

"A simple library for layouting directed graphs. It has minimal configuration options and a
focus on speed over choosing the most optimal layout" [4].

- **Algorithm basis**: Sugiyama/DOT from Graphviz [29]
- **Ranker algorithms**: network-simplex (default), tight-tree, longest-path [29]
- **Status**: v2.0.0 released November 23, 2025 [25]; 5.6k GitHub stars [25]
- **Two npm packages**: only the DagreJs org version receives updates [25]
- **License**: MIT [25]
- **Integration**: Synchronous — compute once, update positions [4]
- **Position anchor**: Center point (must adjust to React Flow's top-left by subtracting
  half width/height) [7]

### Configuration

Key dagre parameters set via `setGraph()` [7]:

- `rankdir`: 'TB' (top-bottom), 'BT', 'LR' (left-right), 'RL' — default TB [29]
- `nodesep`: 50px default — horizontal spacing between nodes [29]
- `ranksep`: 50px default — vertical spacing between ranks [29]
- `edgesep`: 10px default — horizontal edge separation [29]
- Alternative rankers: `tight-tree`, `longest-path` (default network-simplex) [29]

### Performance Concerns

Community report [30]: Dagre ~40× slower than **Cytoscape's breadthfirst layout** with 1,000 nodes and 2,000 edges ("5 sec vs. 3 min" per the reporter's informal timing). Environment was Angular 11 + cytoscape, no styling. Issue remains open, no formal resolution. Designed for medium-sized graphs quickly at cost of optimal layouts [4].

Dagre's own maintenance posture: the DagreJs-org fork released **v2.0.0 on November 23, 2025** [25], contradicting historical community perception of deprecation [47].

## ELK (Eclipse Layout Kernel)

"The most configurable option available, but it's also the most complicated. Elkjs is a
Java library that's been ported to JavaScript" [4].

- **Algorithm**: Layered method based on Sugiyama [9]
- **Ported via**: Google Web Toolkit (GWT) compilation to JavaScript [4]
- **Bundle size**: ~1.4 MB [4]
- **Integration**: Asynchronous (promise-based), supports web workers [8]
- **Maintained by**: KIELER Project (academic research team) [9]

### Core Phases [9]

| Phase | Default Strategy |
|-------|-----------------|
| Cycle Breaking | GREEDY |
| Layering | NETWORK_SIMPLEX |
| Crossing Minimization | LAYER_SWEEP |
| Node Placement | BRANDES_KOEPF |

### Edge Routing Strategies [9]

- **Orthogonal** (default): horizontal/vertical segments, arbitrary port constraints
- **Straight**: direct connections
- **Splines**: curved paths with SLOPPY mode
- **Polyline**: multi-segment routing

### Spacing Defaults [9]

| Parameter | Default |
|-----------|---------|
| Node-to-node | 20 |
| Edge-to-edge | 10 |
| Node-to-node between layers | 20 |
| Port surrounding | 0 |

### Hierarchy Handling

Supports "full layout of compound graphs with cross-hierarchy edges" via INCLUDE_CHILDREN
option [9].

### Configuration

Over 150 configuration options [8]. Common settings [8]:

```
elk.algorithm: 'layered'
elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers: '100'
elk.spacing.nodeNode: '80'
```

Performance tunable via `thoroughness` parameter (1-7, default 7) [9].

## D3-Hierarchy

"Assigns the same width and height to all nodes when calculating the layout" — unsuitable
for mixed node types [4]. Best for simple trees with uniform node dimensions [4].

- **Bundle size**: ~14 KB [4]
- **Limitation**: Single root requirement [4]

## D3-Force

Physics-based force-directed layout using iterative simulation [4].

- **Bundle size**: ~15 KB [4]
- **Integration**: Iterative — uses hooks to update positions across multiple renders [4]
- **Strengths**: Visually interesting, supports interactive dragging [4]
- **Weaknesses**: Computationally expensive, requires performance management [4]

## D3-DAG

Specialized for DAGs (not just trees). Three layout algorithms: Sugiyama, Zherebko (linear
topological), Grid [28]. In "light maintenance mode" — designed for "small to medium sized
static DAGs" [28]. Fluent API with immutable operators [28].

## Real-World Layout Evolution

Pinpoint Engineering's workflow editor evaluated three algorithms sequentially [20]:

1. **d3-hierarchy** (136 KB): worked for linear workflows, "quickly fell short when we
   introduced conditional nodes" [20]
2. **dagre.js**: improved spacing but couldn't handle "fixed node positioning" for
   maintaining branch order [20]
3. **ELK.js** (7.8 MB): final choice with dynamic node sizing, custom spacing, direction
   control, and smooth branching [20]

Their ELK configuration used the 'mrtree' algorithm with 50-unit node spacing [20].

Note: Pinpoint Engineering reports bundle sizes of 136 KB (d3-hierarchy) and 7.8 MB
(ELK) [20], compared to React Flow's documentation listing ~14 KB and ~1.4 MB [4].
The discrepancy likely reflects different measurement scopes — Pinpoint measured total
bundled size including dependencies, while React Flow docs cite library-only sizes.

## Smart Edge Routing

Not built into React Flow. Third-party `react-flow-smart-edge` uses A* pathfinding for
obstacle avoidance with three variants (SmartBezierEdge, SmartStraightEdge, SmartStepEdge) [42]. Built-in `pathfindingAStarDiagonal` (default) and `pathfindingAStarNoDiagonal` implementations; custom pathfinding functions supported [42]. The repository was **archived December 17, 2025** [42]; users seeking maintenance should evaluate current forks.

## Counter-evidence on ELK bundle size (2026-04-19 addition)

ELK's bundle size is a documented community concern. The reaviz/reaflow project opened an issue explicitly attributing their own "huge bundle size" problem to elkjs (sources surfaced by counter-discovery 2026-04-19). An **open issue on the elkjs repo (#6)** requests modularization — the maintainers acknowledge the size problem but the original GWT-to-JavaScript compilation pipeline makes it structurally hard to fix piecemeal. This reinforces the "~1.4 MB is a real deployment concern" side of the Dagre-vs-ELK trade-off and is independent corroboration of [4]'s size warning.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published benchmarks comparing layout algorithms at specific node counts (measured head-to-head)
- d3-hierarchy's uniform sizing makes it unsuitable for most workflow editors [4]
- Dagre's sub-flow support has known connectivity issues [4]
- ELK's 1.4 MB library-only bundle (or 7.8 MB bundled-with-deps per [20]) is a significant trade-off for simple use cases [4]
- No independent head-to-head Dagre vs ELK measured benchmark was found during the 2026-04-19 update — all public comparisons remain qualitative
